_meta.indication: CABLIVI is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with acquired thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (aTTP), in combination with plasma exchange and immunosuppressive therapy.

pivotal_trials.nct: NCT12553315 (as stated in review; TITAN supportive study NCT01151423)
pivotal_trials.design: 1:1 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter study of caplacizumab plus standard of care in acute episodes of aTTP; randomization stratified by Glasgow Coma Scale score.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult (age ≥18 years) patients with a diagnosis of aTTP and platelet count <100,000/µL.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Time to platelet response, defined by platelet count ≥150,000/µL and cessation of daily plasma exchange within 5 days of satisfying the platelet threshold.
pivotal_trials.result: Time to platelet response favored caplacizumab: HR 1.58 (95% CI 1.11, 2.24), log-rank p=0.0099. Key secondary composite endpoint (TTP-related death, TTP recurrence, or major thromboembolic event) 12.5% caplacizumab vs 49.3% placebo, p<0.0001; TTP recurrence over the overall study period 12.5% vs 38.4%, p=0.0004.

key_safety: Most frequent adverse reactions (>15%) were epistaxis, headache, and gingival bleeding (gingival bleeding 16% vs 3% placebo; fatigue 15% vs 9%). Bleeding events occurred in ~58% on CABLIVI vs 43% on placebo; serious bleeding reactions in ≥2% included epistaxis (4%) and subarachnoid hemorrhage (2%).
target_moa: Caplacizumab is a bivalent humanized anti-vWF antibody fragment that binds the A1 domain of von Willebrand Factor and inhibits the interaction between vWF and platelets, thereby reducing vWF-mediated platelet adhesion and formation of microthrombi.

rems.type: No Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy is recommended for caplacizumab for the proposed indication.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting is recommended for this application.

summary.text: CABLIVI (BLA 761112) was approved via a standard (non-accelerated) pathway under Priority Review granted August 1, 2018, with prior Fast Track designation (July 21, 2017) and Orphan Drug Designation (April 14, 2009). Approval was based on the pivotal Phase 3 HERCULES trial. No Advisory Committee meeting and no REMS were required.
